title: The Weekly Design Brief — and your uniforms enter the history books
summary: Two additions for the long haul. Every Monday a new Design Brief lands on the Exchange: a themed styling challenge ("Midnight Classic", "Thunderstorm", "Ghost Corps"…) that scores any of your saved designs automatically against a visible checklist — no judges, no mystery, just a rubric to chase. Your first entry each week earns CorpsCoin, and the week's board is public. And starting with the next season rollover, the uniform you have equipped is stamped into that season's archive: your Corps History timeline now shows the look you wore each season, forever.
highlights: Sixteen briefs rotate weekly; the checklist shows exactly which looks score and for how much.
Resubmit as often as you like — your week's best score stands, and only the first entry pays.
Season archives now carry each corps' equipped uniform: swatches on the timeline, the full figure in the season detail.
Under the hood: equipped uniforms (and alternates) now survive season rollover correctly.

title: The Design Exchange: a public gallery for your uniforms
summary: Your designs can now hang in public. Publish any saved look to the new Design Exchange and every director can browse it, like it, and save a copy into their own wardrobe — with your name attached, and a little CorpsCoin in your pocket each time someone new saves it. Share links got smarter too: paste a uniform link in Discord and it unfurls into a card showing the design's colors and import code.
highlights: Publish from the Studio; browse the gallery at Exchange, sorted by newest or most saved.
Save a copy imports the design into your wardrobe with credit to the designer — remix away.
Designers earn CorpsCoin for each unique save (capped per day, so it stays a thank-you, not a farm).
Get code now copies a share link that unfurls into a design card and lands friends in their own Studio with your design loaded.
Public director pages now show each corps' equipped uniform colors next to its name.

title: Your colors on the scoreboard — and an alternate look
summary: Two finishing touches for uniform identity. Score sheets and season standings now show each corps' equipped colorway as a slim three-color bar beside its name — equip a design and your colors march onto the scoreboard from your next scored show. And every corps gains an optional alternate look: a second equipped uniform for finals week or exhibitions, shown alongside your identity uniform on your profile.
highlights: The colorway bar appears automatically wherever scores and standings render once a design is equipped.
Equip as alt in the Studio sets the second look; Clear alt removes it. Your primary stays the corps' identity everywhere else.
Both looks survive season rollover and retiring/unretiring a corps.

title: The aussie brim sits truer
summary: The aussie slouch hat's brim rode at too steep an angle — the open side drooped. It now sits flatter with the same sweep up into the pinned side, feather and mirror included.

title: Chest badges and the '93 triangle blade
summary: Two long-requested looks from the wishlist thread. Every design can now wear a chest badge — any of the hat ornament shapes (including the new rectangle-in-rectangle patch) in its own two colors, on whichever breast you choose. And the diagonal sash and baldric learned new cuts: the classic band, a tapered wide-to-narrow band, or the triangle blade — the great sweeping shoulder-to-waist triangle with a nested inner triangle and metallic trim edge. The new Ivory Blade preset shows it off in cream, black, and gold.
highlights: Chest badge: pick a shape, a color, an optional detail color, and which breast it sits on — independent of everything else on the jacket.
The rectangle badge shape is also available as a hat ornament.
Sash and baldric shapes: classic band, triangle blade, or tapered. The baldric's center-stripe color doubles as the blade's inner triangle.
Blades and tapered bands still honor the color fade, sequins, and the other-shoulder mirror.

title: The aussie earns its swagger — plus side feathers
summary: The aussie slouch hat got a proper redraw: a taller creased crown, a wide brim that sweeps up into the pinned side, and a badge that sits where it should. New with it: the side feather plume — the classic spray off the lifted brim, with an optional tip color for the dyed-feather look — and a toggle to lift the other side instead, feather and all.

title: The 2000s check in: contour shako, two-tone plumes
summary: Two player requests bridging the era gap between the classics and today's looks. The new contour shako is the tall, sleek, swept-top hat of the 2000s and early 2010s — clean face by default, any ornament and plume optional. Plumes everywhere can now take a second tip color for the classic dyed-feather look. The new Millennium preset puts it all together: navy and silver with a blue-tipped plume.

title: The modern swash, your way — and sequins are always optional
summary: Straight from the Discord: the modern swash now splits into independent torso and leg parts — keep either or both — and its leg band takes its own color. Sequins got a checkbox everywhere they appear: swash, legs, sashes, baldrics, and gauntlets can all go matte. Epaulets were always there but hard to find; the section is now labeled Neck, shoulders & extras.

title: Uniform codes and share cards: your look, everywhere
summary: Your designs can now leave the Studio. Mint a short uniform code (like MA-7K3F-Q2) for any saved look and anyone can type it into their own Studio to import the design — with credit to you. Or export a share card: your corps taking the field in formation under stadium lights, with your name, colorway, and the code stamped on it, ready for Discord.
highlights: Get code copies a short shareable code for the current design; a friend pastes it in the new Import box to load your look as a draft they can save and remix.
Imported designs always show who designed them.
Share card exports a field-entrance PNG — a mixed-tone ensemble wearing your uniform, plus your code so the card is its own invitation.
Design Notes now appear in the editor: one-line principles from the craft, matched to what you're building.

title: Hat ornaments: pick the shape, pick the color — plus the aussie
summary: Headwear got a whole wardrobe of its own. The front ornament on shakos and pith helmets is now selectable — sunburst plate, star, crest shield, chevrons, disc, diamond, or bare — and takes any color you like (asked for by a director who wanted a red cog on the 906 Red Stars shako; clear it to fall back to your hardware metal). And the aussie slouch hat finally marches in: wide brim, pinned-up side, your ornament riding it as a badge.

title: Pick your button color
summary: Buttons on braid rows and double-breasted jackets no longer have to match your hardware metal — give them any color you like, or clear it to fall back to gold or silver.

title: Baldrics your way: either shoulder, two-tone, faded
summary: Straight from a director's wish list: sashes, baldrics, and swashes can now run over the other shoulder with one toggle, baldrics take an optional center-stripe color for that classic two-tone look, and any of the three can fade between two colors from shoulder to hip.

title: Paint your own fade sleeves
summary: Sleeves now have a Color fade option in the Studio: pick a top and bottom color and the sleeve blends between them. Fade each arm independently or keep both linked — your call, like every other piece.

title: Gauntlets now flare the right way
summary: Gauntlets on the Studio figure were drawn upside down — tight mid-arm and flaring toward the hand. They now wear like the real thing: snug at the wrist with the bell opening up the forearm.

title: Recolor every print in the Uniform Studio
summary: The Studio's printed surfaces are no longer stuck in their stock colors. Pick your own hues for the radial burst, the op-art lattice, and the pinstripe — and for plaid and foil legs too. Color pickers appear right under the print you're using, the highlights and shading re-derive to match, and your choices save and equip with the design like any other channel.

title: Uniform Studio scrolls properly on phones
summary: On mobile, the Uniform Studio was stuck on its first screen — you could see your figure but couldn't scroll down to the presets, colors, and piece controls. The page now scrolls end to end, and the preview figure is sized for phone screens so your design tools are right below it.

title: Show Day strip: right show, right encore
summary: Two fixes to the dashboard's Show Day strip. Its "Full schedule & running order" link now opens the running order for the show you're looking at, instead of dropping you on the top of your schedule. And the "You're the encore" banner now only appears when you're actually the encore at that show — it no longer showed up on any show day just because you were the encore somewhere else on your tour.

title: The Studio no longer crashes on split-side arms or legs
summary: Turning off "Link sides" and customizing just one arm or one leg could throw a "Studio Error" that took over the page and forced you to close the tab — and a design saved in that state crashed every time you reopened it. Asymmetric limbs now render cleanly, and any design already saved that way loads and edits normally again.

title: Green Satin preset trades its shako for a white aussie
summary: The Green Satin classic preset now marches in a white aussie slouch hat instead of the black shako — a cleaner, brighter crown over the satin jacket. Load the preset to see the new look, or swap any hat as always.

title: Saving a uniform with a sleeve fade works again
summary: Designs that used a sleeve fade or any gradient failed to save in the Studio with an "INTERNAL (500)" error. Those looks now save, equip, and share like any other — no need to strip the fade first.

title: The Uniform Studio: design your corps' identity, live
summary: Uniform design is no longer a text form — the new Uniform Studio draws your corps as you build it. Pick real drum-corps pieces from shakos and plumes to streamers and sublimated prints, recolor any part, save a wardrobe of looks, and equip the one that is your corps. Your profile now shows every ensemble in its equipped uniform.
highlights: A live figure updates instantly with every choice — no waiting on AI generation.
Real vocabulary from both eras: cadet jackets, braid rows, baldrics, gauntlets and spats beside bodysuit prints, glow piping, tattered hems, and per-side asymmetric looks.
Eleven starting presets across a Heritage line and a Show line — load one, then swap or recolor anything; every piece combines with every piece.
Save up to 24 designs in your wardrobe and equip any of them per corps; equipped uniforms appear on your profile's new Corps Identity section.
The press-box toggle previews your design at field distance — does it read from the stands?
Saving a design no longer regenerates your avatar or changes your profile picture; the AI avatar is now its own optional button.

title: Your show day now leads the dashboard
summary: The dashboard opens with your own show day — which event your corps is at, where, when the show starts, and when you take the field, with a live ticker while the show runs. Works for both the Fantasy and Podium divisions; the full running order lives one tap away on the Schedule page.
highlights: Show days lead with your event, its location, showtime, and your corps' own field time — including an on-field-now countdown while the show is live.
Off days show your next scheduled show instead, and if nothing's booked, a shortcut to pick shows on the schedule.
Podium directors get the same strip, built from the Podium field's own running order and show times.
The full running-order list no longer takes up the bottom of the dashboard — tap through to the Schedule page to see the whole field.

title: Encores come to Podium
summary: The cosmetic encore — one corps named to perform after scores read — now happens on the Podium side too, not just Fantasy. Each side picks its own encore from the corps registered for that show: the hometown corps closest to the venue (or your own corps at a show you host). It never scores or affects standings — it's the pride of seeing your corps take the field one more time. Watch for it on the Podium tab of a show's running order, and in the "You're the encore" banner on your dashboard.

title: System shows get their running order too
summary: Every show now lays out its timed running order once corps register — not just director-hosted ones. Some system-scheduled shows were only showing the attendee list because the schedule treated them as taking place on their original historical date; they now carry their in-game date, so the full performance schedule appears like it does everywhere else.

title: Press releases have their own path to instant publishing
summary: Posting your corps' own news no longer waits on getting news articles approved. Your first few press releases are reviewed by an admin, and once three of them are approved, your releases publish instantly — a trust track separate from news submissions.
highlights: Anyone with a registered corps can write a press release right away — early ones go to review first.
After three approved press releases, new ones publish instantly with no review.
Press-release trust is earned from press releases, not from submitted news articles.

title: Weather is back on the schedule cards
summary: Show cards again display the show-time conditions at each venue — a sky icon and the temperature — so you can see the forecast for a night before you register.

title: See the full running order — and who's on the field right now
summary: Show schedules now lay out the complete running order for every event, built from the real registered field, and a live layer highlights the corps performing right now. Attendee rosters, a Fantasy/Podium view, and finals encores come along too.
highlights: Every show lists its running order, not just a start time.
A live indicator marks the corps currently taking the field.
Attendee rosters now appear on all shows, not only director-hosted ones.
Switch between the Fantasy and Podium fields; finals can close with an encore.

title: The Podium “Lineup” button now opens a real chooser
summary: Clicking “Lineup” on a Podium corps used to do nothing. It now opens a chooser to rehearse or switch your lineup, and it sits centered properly on desktop.

title: Deleting your account now cleans up fully
summary: When you delete your account, your director is anonymized, the corps names you had reserved are freed for others to use, and you are removed from any upcoming show registrations — no lingering traces left behind.

title: Fantasy recap ledger shows the show's location
summary: The fantasy season recap ledger now lists where each show actually took place, instead of mistakenly showing your corps' home city.

title: Real show-time weather on schedules and in articles
summary: Schedule cards now carry the actual forecast for each show's day and time, refreshed the evening before so it's accurate, and generated recaps set the scene with the real conditions on the field.
highlights: Each schedule card shows the day-of forecast for that show.
A late-day refresh keeps conditions current before showtime.
Recap articles open with the real weather at the venue.

title: Season XP now paces across the whole season
summary: The season progression ladder was retuned so leveling stretches across the full season instead of topping out in the early weeks, keeping later-season play rewarding.

title: Corps History reads well on mobile
summary: The Corps History view is now mobile-friendly, and a bug that could list duplicate seasons in a corps' history was fixed.

title: Daily login credited on time everywhere
summary: Players outside UTC no longer have their daily login counted late, so streaks and daily rewards register on the right day no matter your time zone.

title: Podium directors get achievements, titles, and a season recap
summary: Podium-only directors are now full citizens: they earn achievements and prestige titles from their Podium seasons and shows, get a Podium-specific Quick Start walkthrough, and are met with a season-end recap on their next visit instead of having to go hunting for it.
highlights: Podium seasons and shows now count toward the seasons/shows achievements and the titles that gate on them.
New Podium Debut and Open/World Class Director achievements.
Quick Start now teaches the Podium loop — rehearse, register, plan — not the fantasy draft steps.
A season-end Podium recap greets you on your next login and routes into the full between-seasons assessment.

title: Your press releases now post to Discord
summary: Publish a press release for your corps and it now lands in a dedicated Discord channel with a 📣 Press Release marker, so your organization's voice reaches the community where it already talks. Newsroom articles keep flowing to the news channel as before.
highlights: Press releases route to their own channel, separate from newsroom coverage.
Each carries a distinct 📣 "Press Release" label in the embed.

title: A consistent header and a calmer mobile layout
summary: The signed-in header now matches across the app and public pages — the same Discord, inbox, Explore, and help cluster everywhere — and several mobile crowding and overflow issues were cleaned up so the top of the screen stays tidy on a phone.
highlights: Your notification inbox is now reachable from public pages too.
Fixed the mobile header overflow that crowded the signed-in view.
The news category filter no longer overflows on mobile.
The home page now leads with its highest-value content.

title: No more getting bounced to onboarding on mobile
summary: Established directors on a fresh phone, cleared storage, or private mode are no longer wrongly redirected into the welcome/onboarding flow. The app now waits for the server to confirm before deciding you're a new user — a problem that mostly hit mobile.

title: A clearer way around the game
summary: A navigation pass tidied the chrome: game destinations moved out of the ❓ help menu into a dedicated Explore menu, the desktop nav now leads with your daily hub instead of News, Hall of Champions has one canonical home, and the score ticker can be collapsed when you want the quiet.
highlights: Shop, Achievements, Records, and the archives now live under a shared Explore menu.
The ❓ menu is back to pure help — guides, what's new, results, legal.
Desktop and mobile now agree on nav priority, leading with the daily loop.
Collapse the desktop score ticker from the header; the choice sticks.

title: The Podium Report reads like a real column now
summary: The nightly Podium Report was rewritten from a terse, same-every-night recap into a drama-forward feature that tells the day's actual story — a coup at the top, a long reign, the caption kings, the closest race — all still built straight from the standings, no invented numbers.
highlights: Headlines now come from the night's real storyline instead of a fixed "Day N" masthead.
New sections: the caption kings, the closest call, expanded movers, and the floor.
Every beat stays silent when the numbers for it aren't there.

title: Your season, told as a recap ledger
summary: A new season ledger lays out your corps' whole season show-by-show — every scored outing with its full caption breakdown, subtotals, total, and placement, plus season best, average, and medal tally. Added for Podium first, then extended to the fantasy classes.
highlights: Reach it from the Podium Dashboard or by clicking SEASON SCORE on your scorecard.
Each caption's season best is highlighted in gold as a personal box-topper.
Shares as Discord-ready text like the other score sheets.

title: Podium airfare bookings no longer vanish quietly
summary: A booked flight that ended up stranded — its show moved or dropped — is now surfaced to you instead of being silently discarded, so you can see and recover the CorpsCoin you committed.

title: Podium Division scores in the live ticker
summary: The scrolling score ticker now carries the Podium Division alongside the Fantasy Division classes, grouped by class, so the Podium tour gets the same at-a-glance presence as everything else.

title: Corps names are unique across Fantasy and Podium
summary: A corps name is now reserved across both games at creation, so a fantasy corps' name can't be reused for a Podium corps — even your own. That closes a duplicate a nightly cleanup used to have to keep sweeping up.

title: Regional titles go to the right shows
summary: Only the three branded majors — Southwestern, Southeastern, and the two-night Eastern Classic — now crown regional champions. Pool shows that happened to fall on a major's day were wrongly minting trophies; those were stripped and the right champions backfilled, for Fantasy and Podium.
highlights: Podium now crowns one overall regional champion per major.
Existing recaps were corrected retroactively, so past regionals read right.

title: Open and A Class champions come from their own Finals
summary: The Hall of Champions now crowns Open Class and A Class champions from the Day 46 Open/A Class Finals — their own title night — instead of their placement in the Day 49 World Championship bracket. World Class still settles on Day 49.

title: The Fan Favorite crown lands in your trophy case
summary: The Podium Fan Favorite winner now gets a distinct pink Heart in the profile trophy case — separate from every competitive medal — carrying the crowned corps, season, and winning vote count. A season-defining honor, never a placement.

title: Six new corps card themes in the shop
summary: More ways to spend CorpsCoin on your corps' look: six new card themes across the price tiers, including the two most-requested — Fogwalker Teal and Evergreen.
highlights: New: Fogwalker Teal, Evergreen, Slate Graphite, Amethyst, Rose Quartz, and Glacier.

title: Podium and Fantasy now read as two distinct games
summary: The dashboard, Game Guide, and Records now clearly separate the Podium director sim from the fantasy draft, so a Podium mark is never mistaken for a fantasy-comparable one. A banner on the Podium zone names the boundary — and you can dismiss it for good once you know the ropes.
highlights: Tabs group the four Fantasy classes apart from Podium, which keeps its gold Medal identity.
The Game Guide rail is grouped into Start here / Fantasy / Systems / Podium / Reference.
Records and profile ensembles separate Fantasy and Podium results.
The Podium mode banner is now permanently dismissible.

title: Book airfare for long Podium tour legs
summary: Podium directors can now pre-book a flight on any upcoming show leg over the long-haul distance, halving that leg's travel-stamina hit for a CorpsCoin fare. Fly the brutal jumps and drive the rest.
highlights: Priced at 1 CorpsCoin per 2 leg-miles, charged from your Corps Budget.
Booked per day from the Upcoming Route panel, and fully reversible.
Stacks with the Tour Manager reduction; if the Budget can't cover it, you simply drive.

title: Champions show their corps graphics
summary: The Hall of Champions now displays each champion and finalist with their corps graphic instead of a bare initial — and past seasons were backfilled, so older champions get their logos too.

title: Joint rehearsals no longer relocate the tour route
summary: Joint rehearsals no longer relocate the tour route

title: Podium corps now have a home city
summary: Podium setup now asks for an official home city; every tour starts there and each travel leg is priced from it. Continuing directors can relocate at the start of a season for a per-mile fee — founding or keeping your home is free.
highlights: Your home shows as a standardized "City, ST" on the profile and anchors the tour map.
Relocation costs 1 CorpsCoin per 2 miles from your old home, previewed before you commit.
Podium corps are now correctly eligible for director-hosted shows everywhere they're listed.

title: Sharper, more accurate scores
summary: The fantasy and Podium score engines now ignore malformed historical values — stray totals landing in caption fields, and un-scored zeros — that were skewing projections and dragging Podium's realism curves. The scores you see track real results more faithfully.

title: Podium show picks stay put mid-week
summary: Editing a week's Podium show picks no longer silently drops shows you've already performed. That closes a loophole that let a corps attend more shows than the weekly cap allows, and keeps completed shows plotted on your tour map.

title: Prestige titles are a career, not a sprint
summary: The top director titles — Icon, Hall of Famer, Immortal, and Eternal — now require completed seasons as well as XP, so Hall of Fame status is a long-haul achievement instead of something reachable in two seasons.
highlights: Legend stays a pure Level-10 milestone; higher tiers add a seasons-played bar.
Matching level achievements gain the same gate; badges you've already earned are never revoked.

title: Podium-only directors can post press releases
summary: If your only corps is a Podium corps, the press-release composer no longer turns you away with "Register a corps first." Your Podium corps is now a valid byline.

title: Podium clinician boost ends on schedule
summary: A clinician engagement now clears the moment its last active day finishes, instead of lingering an extra day. The "active through day N" panel disappears exactly when the boost does.

title: A Newsroom and writer credentials on your profile
summary: Your director profile gained a Newsroom that gathers the press releases and articles you've published, plus an earned writer tier shown as a badge. Credentials come from real contributions, not a grant.
highlights: The tier climbs Contributor → Correspondent → Staff Writer.
Admin-approved articles are weighted above self-published releases, so the top tier can't be farmed on volume.

title: Post press releases for your corps
summary: Your organization now has a voice. Publish press releases about your own corps — instantly, no review — and they land in the news feed under your byline.
highlights: Share reveals, staff moves, results, and rivalries from your corps’ point of view.
Publishes the moment you post it, with a PRESS RELEASE badge in the feed.
Distinct from Submit an Article, which covers the wider circuit and is reviewed.
You can remove your own releases at any time.

title: Podium veterans start closer to form
summary: A returning Podium corps now opens the season with a head start scaled to how engaged it was last season, so continuity is rewarded without erasing the climb.

title: A sharper daily loop
summary: The daily challenges were rebuilt around real same-day actions, with clearer XP and a weekly streak that pays out as you go.
highlights: Challenges now track genuine actions you take that day.
Tiered XP: 10 for a core challenge, 20 for the daily stretch.
The weekly arc is a graduated ladder — rewards at 3, 5, and 7 active days.

title: Director-hosted shows, clearer schedules
summary: Podium hosting and the schedule got a polish pass: director-hosted shows are called out and detailed, venues resolve to standardized "City, ST" locations, and Podium scores nightly at 9 PM ET year-round.
highlights: Hosted shows show the hosting director and full rosters, Podium corps included.
Schedule locations standardized to two-letter state codes.
Podium classes are seated at the reset so promotions reach scoring.

title: Podium: season assessment & a feature-length Report
summary: Podium gained a season-start assessment and corps-lifecycle decisions at registration, and the daily Podium Report was rewritten as a full power-rankings column.

title: Finals night scores now reveal
summary: Day 49 finals scores in the Fantasy classes now reveal correctly, so the season closes on the result it should.

title: Score-drop alerts & shareable score cards
summary: The nightly score drop finally reaches you: a morning push when results land, a Discord embed, and shareable score cards with public, crawlable results pages behind every link.
highlights: Morning notification when the night’s scores publish.
Share a score and it opens a public results page for that day.
Legacy Endowments added a lasting, commemorative way to spend CorpsCoin.

title: Your show history shows what you earned
summary: Your director profile's show history now lists the CorpsCoin you took home from each show, so your competitive record and your budget tell one story.

title: Leagues get a clubhouse
summary: Your league now has a clubhouse — a shared home with clearer standings, easier invitations, and better visibility into what your league-mates are up to.

title: Community polls now post to Discord
summary: Site polls now cross-post to Discord so the whole community can weigh in where it already gathers, with the results flowing back to the site.

title: Reset a forgotten password
summary: Locked out? You can now recover your account with a password reset instead of being stuck at the sign-in screen.

title: Cleaner corps creation
summary: Creating a corps now catches duplicate and invalid names up front, so you don't lose your setup to an error after the fact.

title: See your corps' trajectory over time
summary: A new progression history charts your corps season over season, so you can watch your program's arc — not just tonight's score.

title: Buy Me a Coffee supporter tiers
summary: marching.art is donation-only — nothing about the game is gated behind money. If you'd like to chip in, new Buy Me a Coffee supporter tiers add a thank-you in the form of profile flair and a spot on the Supporters wall.
highlights: Supporting is entirely optional; no gameplay is locked behind it.
Always-on supporter flair shows on your profile.
A Supporters wall recognizes everyone who chips in.

title: Introducing Podium: direct your own corps
summary: Podium is a whole new way to play — a director's sim where you run a single corps of your own: register it, plan its rehearsals, tour a real calendar of shows, and get scored every night. It runs alongside the fantasy game and is always open to join.
highlights: A guided registration wizard and rehearsal planner get you on the field.
Your corps competes on the nightly Podium stage against other directors.
Tour a season calendar anchored to the real majors, regionals, and championship weeks.
A two-level Fan Favorite community ballot crowns a season favorite.

title: A redesigned trophy case
summary: The profile trophy case was rebuilt as clean, class-distinct icon chips — the shape tells the class, the color tells the award — so a whole career of results reads at a glance.

title: League prediction pools
summary: Put your read on the season to work: league prediction pools let you and your league-mates wager CorpsCoin on outcomes — the flagship social way to spend what you earn.

title: SoundSport joins daily predictions
summary: The daily prediction game now includes SoundSport with placement-style questions, so there's more of the circuit to call each day.

title: Daily predictions, saved and rewarded
summary: Your daily predictions now save reliably and pay out accuracy bonuses, so calling the night right earns you CorpsCoin.

title: A First Season Journey for new directors
summary: New directors get a First Season Journey questline and a rookie league placement — a guided path through your opening season instead of a blank slate.

title: Clearer deadlines and scoring cadence
summary: The game now surfaces when things are due and when scores drop across the app, alongside a mobile and accessibility polish pass so it all reads well on a phone.
highlights: Deadlines and scoring times are called out where you need them.
Lineup and score tables no longer clip off-screen on mobile.
An accessibility and reduced-motion pass across the site.

title: World and Open corps earn show CorpsCoin
summary: World and Open class corps are now paid their show-participation CorpsCoin like everyone else, closing a gap where competing didn't pay out.

title: The live season is here
summary: marching.art now runs alongside the real season: schedules mirror the actual tour, and each night's results and coverage are built from that night's real scores as they land.
highlights: Live Scores show current-year rankings as the season unfolds.
The schedule tracks the real tour, spring training included.
Nightly articles are written from that night's real results.
Last season's articles stay readable after the season resets.

title: Sharper nightly corps images
summary: The images generated for your corps each night got a quality upgrade, so your corps looks its best in the news feed and on your profile.

title: Your customizations stick across seasons
summary: World and Open profile ensembles and the customizations you set now carry across a season reset instead of reverting.

title: The draft pool focuses on attainable corps
summary: Very high point-value corps are no longer offered in the lineup draft, keeping the draftable pool centered on realistic picks.

title: Retire, transfer, or revive a corps mid-season
summary: You can now retire a corps, transfer it, or bring a retired one back during the season — as long as it hasn't competed yet — instead of waiting for the offseason to reshape your roster.

title: New dashboard panels: predictions, lineup analyzer, achievements
summary: The dashboard gained three at-a-glance panels: a Daily Predictions mini-game, a Lineup Analyzer to weigh your caption picks, and an Achievement Tracker for your progress.
highlights: Daily Predictions: call the day's outcomes right from your dashboard.
Lineup Analyzer: see how your caption choices stack up.
Achievement Tracker: watch your milestones fill in.

title: More cinematic corps imagery
summary: The images that illustrate your corps and the news feed were reworked from wide stadium shots into intimate, close-up photojournalism, so the coverage reads like real field photography.

title: Move a corps between classes
summary: You can now transfer a corps to a different class, so your program isn't locked to the class it was founded in.

title: Classes unlock over time, not just by XP
summary: Higher classes now open up on a time basis alongside XP and CorpsCoin, so steady play earns you access even when you're not grinding progression.

title: Try marching.art before you sign up
summary: New visitors can now explore the game in a Guest Preview without an account, with a How It Works walkthrough and plain-language tooltips for the drum-corps jargon — so you can see what it's about before committing.
highlights: Preview the dashboard and the game as a guest, no sign-up required.
A How It Works section explains the game at a glance.
Tooltips decode caption and scoring jargon in place.

title: An integrated Game Guide
summary: A full Game Guide is now built into the site, reachable from the help icon anywhere, so the rules, scoring, and systems are always a click away.

title: Avatars and uniform design
summary: Make your corps and director your own: choose a profile avatar, give your corps its own avatar, and design uniforms you can copy across your ensembles. Profiles were rebuilt as a Director Career Portfolio.
highlights: Pick and regenerate a profile avatar.
Corps avatars now show on the Scores page.
Design a uniform and copy it across your ensembles.

title: League matchups and weekly recaps
summary: Leagues became a weekly competition: automated head-to-head matchups and a weekly recap, with the leagues page redesigned around a dashboard-first, tabbed layout.

title: Watch real corps performances
summary: You can now search for and watch real drum corps performance videos right inside the game — from the live scores, the standings, and articles — so a score line is one click from the show itself.
